question.problem: A rock band performed at two sold-out concerts. The first concert took place in a location with a $10,000$ people capacity. If the second location's capacity was $115%$ of the first location's capacity, what is the capacity of the second location?
question.worked_solution:
To solve this problem, we can use the formula:

$$
\text{part}=\text{percentage}\times \text{whole}
$$

In our case, the whole is the capacity of the first location, which is $10,000$ people. The percentage is $115%,$ and the part is the capacity of the second location.

**Method 1**

First, we convert the percentage to a decimal:

$$
115%=115÷100=1.15
$$

Applying our formula, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{part} & =\text{percentage}\times \text{whole} \\  & =115%\times 10,000 \\  & =1.15\times 10,000 \\  & =11,500\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $115%$ of $10,000$ is $11,500.$ So, the second location has a capacity of $11,500$ people.

**Method 2**

First, we convert the percentage to a fraction:

$$
115%=\frac{115}{100}=\frac{115÷5}{100÷5}=\frac{23}{20}
$$

Applying our formula, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{part} & =\text{percentage}\times \text{whole} \\  & =115%\times 10,000 \\  & =\frac{23}{20}\times 10,000 \\  & =23\times \frac{10,000}{20} \\  & =23\times 500 \\  & =11,500\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $115%$ of $10,000$ is $11,500.$ So, the second location has a capacity of $11,500$ people.
